content: 1. Conjugated synthetic estrogens can reduce the effects of insulin degludec and insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction may impair glucose tolerance. Close monitoring of glycemic control is recommended when these agents are co-administered. 2. Conjugated synthetic estrogens may decrease the effects of inhaled insulin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction can also impair glucose tolerance. Caution is advised, and glycemic control should be closely monitored. 3. Conjugated synthetic estrogens can reduce the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored closely. 4. Isoniazid may increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 5. Istradefylline can increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical trials have shown that istradefylline at 40 mg/day increases the peak levels and area under the curve (AUC) of CYP3A4 substrates, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose adjustments of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary, and close monitoring is advised. 6. Itraconazole can increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored closely. 7. Ivosidenib can decrease the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be avoided, or alternative therapies should be considered. If co-administration is unavoidable, patients should be monitored for reduced therapeutic effects. 8. Ketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 9. Conjugated synthetic estrogens may decrease the levels of L-methylfolate by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 10. Conjugated synthetic estrogens can reduce the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored closely. 11. Lapatinib can increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 12. Larotrectinib may increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 13. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the levels of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. This interaction may increase the risk of adverse reactions. Close monitoring is recommended. 14. Levofloxacin can decrease the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 15. Levoketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 16. Conjugated synthetic estrogens may increase the levels or effects of linagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative treatments are strongly recommended when linagliptin is co-administered with a CYP3A4 inducer. Close monitoring is advised. 17. Linezolid can decrease the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 18. Conjugated synthetic estrogens can reduce the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic agents. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 19. Conjugated synthetic estrogens may interact with lofepramine through an unspecified mechanism. Estrogens and progestins may reduce the effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and adverse effects. Close monitoring is recommended. 20. Conjugated synthetic estrogens can decrease the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response. Patients receiving oral estrogen replacement may require higher doses of lonapegsomatropin. Close monitoring is recommended.
